newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to license scrap metal exports.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to license scrap metal exports.

text.p: A powerful Russian government commission rejected an Industry Ministry proposal for quotas on exports of scrap non-ferrous and ferrous metals, but plans to license them, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.
It said that a closed meeting of the Current Issues Commission, chaired by First Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Bolshakov, rebuffed the Industry Ministry's quota suggestion.
But Interfax said Bolshakov had ordered various ministries to prepare a government decree within two weeks that would introduce a licence system for all scrap metal exports.
Deputy Industry Minister Serafim Afonin had proposed limiting all scrap metal exports to two million tonnes a year to ensure greater supplies for domestic metals firms.
Interfax quoted State Customs Committee data as showing scrap copper exports over the first half of 1996 were 54,000 tonnes, which it described as a 70 percent rise on total 1995 exports.
London traders said last week that Russian scrap copper availability had been reduced to virtually nothing as supplies dried up.
